messages:
alex-support: FYI — customer ACME reported sudden p99 spikes (~3x) for short prompts on hosted continuous-batching route. They say it started after deploy 3.2.1. Request IDs: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0a1b2c3e. Attaching their sample API call and observed latencies.
alex-support: payload: {\"model\":\"redwood-guest-16k\", \"input\":\"summarize: 2-line\"}  — p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 300ms, p99 up to 2.1s
maya-sre: looking. Do we have any matching infra alerts? ops-bot, can you pull p99 for route /v1/generate for the last hour? :mag_right:
ops-bot: /metrics query: route=\"/v1/generate\" AND model=\"redwood-guest-16k\" | timeframe=1h -> p99 increased from 310ms to 1.9s at 2026-03-16T21:02:00Z (spike lasts ~17min)
lin-platform: 3.2.1 included a tweak to continuous-batcher: changed default coalesce_timeout_ms from 12 -> 20 and enabled adaptive_coalesce=true in canary. Could be related.
maya-sre: that sounds plausible — longer coalesce can increase tail for tiny prompts if a few large requests block the batch. Any tenant-specific overrides? alex-support, did ACME use dedicated or hosted? 
alex-support: hosted, standard plan. No tenant override noted.
maya-sre: repro steps I'll try: send high-rate tiny prompts + a few large ones and watch hold-window interactions.
maya-sre: quick repro script (local):

```bash
# burst of small requests then occasional big request
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-guest-16k\",\"input\":\"short\"}' &
  if (( i % 50 == 0 )); then
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-guest-16k\",\"input\":\"long \"$(yes \"word\" | head -n 200)}'
  fi
done
```

maya-sre: on my dev cluster I see p99 climb when a large request enters a batching worker that already has tiny requests queued — KV cache refill and compute pre-emption cause tail.
lin-platform: config snippet we pushed in 3.2.1:

```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  coalesce_timeout_ms: 20
  max_batch_tokens: 10240
  max_items_per_batch: 64
  adaptive_coalesce: true
```

maya-sre: immediate mitigation options:
- roll back coalesce_timeout_ms to 12ms for canary and monitor
- enforce max_items_per_batch=32 for hosted tier to reduce head-of-line blocking
- enable \"size-aware-routing\": prefer batching workers that are not currently serving large sequences

alex-support: customer asks for workaround now — can we suggest a client-side change? or a server-side hotfix?
lin-platform: client-side: suggest adding a small jittered delay for requests (5–10ms) to de-correlate bursts; not ideal. Server-side: hotpatch to revert coalesce timeout for standard routing and set max_items_per_batch cap.
maya-sre: I'm going to roll a short-lived canary: revert coalesce_timeout_ms -> 12 on 5% of traffic for standard route and set max_items_per_batch=32. Monitoring dashboard alerting on p99 will be updated to 10min rolling.
ops-bot: canary rollout started: config=continuous_batcher.canary-3a -> targets=5% route=/v1/generate
alex-support: I'll loop in customer and propose the temporary workaround and ETA. Thanks.
maya-sre: follow-up: found one more contributor — older workers had kernel scheduling preemption that affects long requests. Will include a patch to prioritize finishing queued tiny batches before accepting a large one (fairness fix) in next minor release.
lin-platform: noted — prepping an emergency changelog. We'll schedule a full rollback if canary doesn't reduce p99 in 30min.
alex-support: customer replied: \"appreciate quick action — will monitor and report.\" :thumbsup:
maya-sre: update (T+18m): canary 5% p99 down from 1.9s -> 360ms. rolling to 25% now.
ops-bot: rollout update: 25% -> 60% -> target 100% pending 30m stability window.
maya-sre: filing follow-up ticket ENG-PLAT-7281 for fairness-fix + longer-term telemetry (request-size histograms per worker).
